newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firms on arrear payments, before T-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firms on arrear payments, before T-bill sale.

text.p: The rouble firmed in lively trade on Tuesday as banks sought funds to make transfers for wage and pension payments and participate in Wednesday's government bond sales, dealers said.
On Wednesday, January 15, the central bank is auctioning 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month paper and three trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ bonds.
roubles/dollar Jan 14 midday Jan 14 early Jan 13 close

"Roubles had been in surplus all January until yesterday but today, major banks which handle state budget funds were selling dollars actively. It looked like the roubles they got were meant to leave the market," one dealer said.
Banks appeared to be buying roubles to pay off wage and pension arrears for which government funds had been allocated.
Dealers said other factors could also be pushing up the rouble.

"Overnight rates rose ahead of the auctions and those of the dollar edged down...But the rouble's firmness may be due to other reasons such as dollar investments and what we see now is a correction," an ABN Amro Bank dealer said.
